title: SELinux
subtitle: MAC modes, config, booleans, and contexts — flip to reveal meaning, example, and notes

cards.meaning: DAC = owner decides (chmod/chown); MAC = system policy decides by label
cards.example: chmod 777 still denied for httpd if policy forbids that path
cards.notes: Both must say yes. SELinux sits on top of the permission model you already know.

cards.meaning: Policy loaded and applied — unauthorized access is blocked and logged
cards.notes: Memory hook: lock the door. Success checks in labs must stay enforcing — permissive-only “fixes” do not count.

cards.meaning: Policy loaded but not enforced — everything allowed; violations still logged
cards.notes: Door open, but write down who tried the lock. Use before enforcing when enabling.

cards.meaning: No SELinux policy loaded — no decisions, no SELinux logs
cards.notes: Course labs often start here. Cannot setenforce from fully disabled — need config + reboot (often a relabel).

cards.meaning: Current mode short vs longer status (policy, mode, config)
cards.notes: getenforce/sestatus = now. /etc/selinux/config = boot default after reboot.

cards.meaning: Boot defaults: SELINUX= mode and SELINUXTYPE= policy type
cards.notes: On RHEL, /etc/sysconfig/selinux is often the same file (symlink). Mode enable/disable needs reboot.

cards.meaning: Temporary enforcing (1) or permissive (0) when SELinux is already enabled
cards.notes: Does not work from Disabled. Does not change the boot default in the config file.

cards.meaning: targeted = jail usual daemons; minimum = smaller set; mls = multi-level security
cards.notes: targeted is the default on ordinary servers. mls is rare (strict classifications).

cards.meaning: Set permissive in config → reboot → watch logs → then enforcing → reboot
cards.notes: Do not jump disabled → enforcing on a box you need. First enable often needs a filesystem relabel.

cards.meaning: Security identity on files/processes that policy matches against (user:role:type:…)
cards.notes: Type is what most targeted policy cares about (e.g. httpd_sys_content_t). Wrong type → deny even if DAC allows.

cards.meaning: Show file SELinux contexts (inspect before changing)
cards.notes: Prefer for reading contexts. Compare expected web content type vs a wrong type like default_t.

cards.meaning: Temporarily change a file’s SELinux context (label)
cards.notes: Fix without turning SELinux off. A restore/relabel can wipe a chcon-only change — make it permanent when needed.

cards.meaning: Reset labels on a path to the policy’s default file-context mapping
cards.notes: Uses the permanent fcontext database. If mapping is wrong, restorecon puts the wrong type back.

cards.meaning: Permanent path→type mapping so labels survive a full restore
cards.notes: Lab idea: temporary chcon drifts after restore; permanent fcontext keeps the custom path correct under enforcing.

cards.meaning: Named on/off policy knobs without writing new policy
cards.notes: semanage boolean -l shows (current, default). setsebool alone lasts until reboot; setsebool -P persists.

cards.meaning: List policy modules loaded in memory
cards.notes: Modular policy packs (apache, antivirus, …). Booleans flip switches inside those packs.
